Cross-repo change for core work item CG-0MUNC7FK5001T5CP (F7: Main Street first consumer).

Adds src/MainStreetAchievements.ts mapping the 12 CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES ids to persistent achievements via the engine-generic @core-engine/AchievementSystem, wired into the challenge completion callback in MainStreetChallenges.ts. No Steam SDK code in this repo; the sink resolves to the renderer IPC client in the Electron launcher and to a no-op elsewhere.

Updates the core submodule to a commit containing the achievement layer (F3) and renderer client (F6). Adds tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts (mapping completeness, launcher-manifest drift guard, idempotent unlock, sink delegation, completion-path wiring).

Core parent: CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MainStreetAchievements.ts` declares an achievement manifest mapping all 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` ids to achievement ids with titles, descriptions, and hidden flags; an automated test asserts every template is mapped exactly once.
- [ ] Challenge completion (including the mid-turn `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` path) unlocks the mapped achievement through the engine `AchievementSystem` exactly once per run, with no Steam SDK import anywhere in this repo.
- [ ] In the Electron launcher the unlock is forwarded over the F6 renderer client; in the browser and headless builds it uses the no-op or local sink and the game stays fully playable.
- [ ] Unit tests in the game repo cover mapping completeness, idempotent unlock, and sink delegation; they pass under `--project unit`.
- [ ] The mapping is validated against the launcher manifest (F4) so drift fails an automated check; the cross-repo change is committed and pushed to the game repo's `dev` branch only.

# Decouple the storyline doc-drift guard from engine-owned heading text

**Headline:** `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b pins literal Markdown headings of the engine-owned reference `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (a git submodule that dev builds advance to the engine's latest dev tip), so any engine-side heading rename silently reddens this game's unit suite. Replace the heading pins with semantic anchors (API symbols, link resolution) plus a rename-tolerant section-structure check, and document why headings are not a cross-repo contract.

discovered-from: MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L

## Problem statement

Dev builds (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) compose the **latest** engine dev tip via `git submodule update --remote core`, not the pinned release SHA. When core (dev tip `01d6bcc1`) renamed `## Engine adapter` → `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` in `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, the game's doc-drift guard (AC5b) reddened on **every** dev build, for **every** game repo that pins those headings — even though nothing in Main Street changed. The inline fix (commit `9f2c6185`) asserted the new heading, but the underlying coupling remains: a heading is an implementation detail of the engine's prose, not a contract the game depends on.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer**, when I bump or dev-sync the engine, I want `npm test` to fail only for genuine breakage, so a green suite is trustworthy and a red suite means something real.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the doc guard to still fail loudly if the engine reference the game's adapters link to disappears or stops documenting the seam API, so releases cannot silently ship against vanished docs.
- As the **producer/operator**, I want the cross-repo doc dependency to be explicit and cheap to maintain, so a rename is a no-op (or a documented one-line change), not a cross-repo firefight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No literal engine heading pins.** The AC5b block in `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` no longer asserts literal section-heading text of `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`; instead it asserts the semantic anchors the game genuinely depends on: the core reference exists, documents `createStorylineSystem` and the `@story-line` package, and names the `GymStorylineScene` consumer (any of these removed → guard fails).
- **AC2 — Rename tolerance is proven by a fixture test.** A new unit test in the same file feeds a fixture copy of the core doc with section headings renamed (e.g. `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` → `## Renamed seam section`) and asserts the contract check still passes; a negative fixture (missing `createStorylineSystem`) asserts the check still fails. *Metric: run the two fixture cases — tolerance passes, regression fails.*
- **AC3 — Link resolution preserved.** The guard keeps asserting that `docs/game/storylines.md` links to `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and that the target resolves on disk, and that the core reference is linked from `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- **AC4 — Failure messages and rationale.** Any guard failure names the offending file and the missing anchor, and the test header comment explains that engine doc headings are not a cross-repo contract and cites this work item (`MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O`); a corresponding one-line note is added near the "thin adapters" paragraph of `docs/game/storylines.md` and under the `## Tests` heading in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` so the next engineer does not re-pin headings. *Metric: a reading of the header comment + both doc notes shows the work-item id and the "headings are not a contract" statement.*
- **AC5 — Engine-revision tolerant and suite green.** The changed test scope passes with the submodule at the pinned SHA and with the engine dev tip the build composes; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Game-side change only — do **not** edit files inside `core/` (engine-owned submodule, re-scaffolded by the game-repo scaffold); if an engine-side fix is later chosen, it is an engine-repo (CG) work item.
- Do not weaken the guard into a no-op: negative cases (missing file, missing symbol, broken link) must still fail the suite.
- No new dependencies; keep the guard in plain vitest + `node:fs`, consistent with the file's existing style.
- Do not change `configs/engine-pin.json` or the `core` gitlink as part of this work (they already agree at dev HEAD: pin `40f83b986a6578b3887dcda8857dd5ee7aa15e57` == gitlink `40f83b98`, re-pinned by commit `5b2ddf72`; the pair moves together on every dev build, so treat the exact SHA as illustrative, not a constant).

## Existing state

- Guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, AC5b block asserts `['## API', '## Authoring seams', '## UI adapter', '## Gym demo']` against `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (created by MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY / MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR; heading pin baked in by commit `9f2c6185`).
- Engine doc at current pin (`40f83b98`) has sections: API, Validation, Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author), Editor (visual authoring tool), Engine adapter, UI adapter, Gym demo, Testing. Note both `## Authoring seams …` and `## Engine adapter` exist at this revision — proof that pinning either name is fragile; the guard must not depend on heading text at all.
- The engine repo currently has **no** docs-consistency test and **no** heading anchor manifest (verified: no engine tests reference `docs/core-engine`, no anchor file) — so "engine owns the contract" would be net-new engine work.
- Sibling churn pattern already fixed inline: MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (pin/pointer mismatch when dev sync advances the submodule during a build).

## Desired change

1. Refactor the AC5b assertions into a small pure helper `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc: string, headers: {file: string; link: boolean}): string[]` (returns missing anchors), so the same logic runs against the real file and against fixtures.
2. Replace the `['## API', …]` heading pins with: file-exists + `createStorylineSystem`/`@story-line`/`GymStorylineScene` presence + a structural check that the doc "documents the section topics" without pinning exact heading text (e.g. each required topic keyword found somewhere in the doc, tolerant of heading renames).
3. Add fixture-driven tests for rename tolerance (pass) and missing-symbol regression (fail).
4. Update the test header comment + the two doc notes (AC4).

## Implementation plan (single vertical slice)

This is a **leaf `task`**, not an epic: one test file plus two one-line doc notes. It is
small enough (effort `Small`, risk `Medium`) that phasing adds ceremony without value, so it is
implemented as a **single vertical slice** (code/guard + tests + docs in one change set) rather
than decomposed into child work items. Within that slice the order preserves test-first
verification: the new contract check is written so its tolerance/regression fixtures fail before
the old heading pins are removed, then the pins are replaced, then the docs notes land.

1. Extract the AC5b assertions into `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc, headers)` returning a
   list of missing anchors (pure, no `fs` inside) — AC1 groundwork, keeps the real-file and
   fixture paths on the same logic.
2. Add the fixture tests first and watch them fail against the current heading-pinned helper:
   renamed-heading fixture passes, `createStorylineSystem`-missing fixture fails — AC2.
3. Replace the `['## API', …]` pins with file-exists + `createStorylineSystem` / `@story-line` /
   `GymStorylineScene` + rename-tolerant section-topic check, calling the helper — AC1, AC3.
4. Update the header comment and the two doc notes with the work-item id — AC4.
5. Verify with the changed-scope test run at the current checkout, then the full suite — AC5.
6. Finish with the standard implementation close-out (build → test → commit in that order).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — AC5b block rewrite, tolerance/regression fixture tests, header rationale.
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/storyline-core-doc-renamed-heading.md` (new) — fixture mirroring the current core doc with headings renamed; or an inline string fixture to avoid duplicating a 400-line doc. Prefer the smallest fixture that provably exercises the renames; if inline, note that it must be refreshed on engine doc content changes.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — one-line note that the guard asserts semantic anchors, not engine heading text.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — one-line note under "Tests" about the engine-doc heading non-contract.
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink — read-only references; must not be edited here.

## Related work

- MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR — created AC5b ("Storyline docs and drift guards", completed).
- MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY — canonical docs + doc-drift guard (completed).
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — browser-wait soak child where this was discovered (completed).
- MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F — sibling pin/pointer churn from dev-sync submodule advance (completed) — same root-cause class.
- MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV — open sibling that makes the composed engine explicit and fails when worktree `./core` lags the pin (complementary: this item makes the guard tolerant of the composed engine's docs).
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED — origin of dev-sync-on-build policy (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the more thorough option — "the cross-repo doc contract should be owned by the engine (stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest)" — is deliberately **out of scope** here: it is net-new engine (CG) work affecting every game repo, and it is a producer decision. It is recorded as an open question in the Appendix; if approved, file a separate CG work item. This item stays game-side and is a prerequisite/valid regardless of that decision.
- **Assumption:** semantic symbols (`createStorylineSystem`, `@story-line`, `GymStorylineScene`) are stable markers of the seam API the game links to; the tolerance fixture must keep the renamed headings under the current section topics so it stays representative.
- **Risk — over-loosening:** a rename-tolerant check can drift into a no-op. Mitigated by AC2's negative fixture and AC3's link-resolution assertions.
- **Assumption:** dev builds keep composing the engine dev tip (policy from MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED); the guard must therefore tolerate any dev-tip doc revision.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-10-25): "Should the cross-repo doc contract be owned by the engine (e.g. a stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest), rather than pinned by game tests?" — **OPEN QUESTION** — routed to producer for decision; **Recommended:** keep this item game-side (semantic anchors + rename tolerance), and file the engine-owned-contract option as a separate engine-repo (CG) work item only if the producer opts in — rationale: a heading is an implementation detail of engine prose, not a contract; semantic API symbols plus link resolution cover what games genuinely depend on, and any engine-side contract is net-new engine work hitting every game repo. Source: work-item description ("Follow-up worth deciding…"), research: engine repo has no docs-consistency test and no anchor manifest today; game repo cannot edit `core/`.
- Q2 (2026-10-25): "Should this item also fix the pin/pointer churn class (dev-sync advancing the submodule during builds)?" — Answer (triage): No — that is MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (already fixed inline) / MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV (open); linked as related work above. Source: work-item + worklog search.
- Q3 (2026-10-27, plan session): "Does the plan need an interview round of its own?" — Answer (agent, from repo + work-item evidence): No. The intake already captured requirements, ACs, constraints, key files and risks, and the plan session only re-validated them against dev HEAD (`tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b, `configs/engine-pin.json` + `core` gitlink at `40f83b98`, `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` `## Tests`, `docs/game/storylines.md` §9 "thin adapters"). Evidence: the seed description plus the git log entries `5b2ddf72` and `9f2c6185`.
- Q1 status (2026-10-27, plan session): still **OPEN QUESTION** for the producer (engine-owned heading/anchor contract), but **not blocking** — the game-side scoped fix is a prerequisite under either answer, so planning completed without a producer handoff. If the producer opts in later, file a separate engine-repo (CG) work item and link it as related work.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-27 — plan session (Map): re-validated the seed description against the repo at dev HEAD.
  Corrections: engine pin/gitlink pair has advanced `9ee194e0` → `40f83b98` (commit `5b2ddf72`);
  the core doc at that revision carries *both* `## Authoring seams …` and `## Engine adapter`, which
  strengthens the no-heading-pins rationale. AC4 tightened to a checkable metric (work-item id in
  the header comment + notes under `## Tests`). Added the single-vertical-slice implementation plan
  and the phasing decision. No children created (leaf task); no interview questions re-asked.

## Review log

- Finished requirements & AC alignment review (plan): AC1–AC5 each trace to the problem statement
  and the "Desired change" list; AC3 absorbs the pre-existing DEVELOPER.md / GYM_INDEX.md and
  link-resolution assertions so nothing is lost when AC5b is rewritten. No invented requirements.
- Finished completeness review (plan): `**Key Files:**` validated (`validate_key_files_format` → no
  issues); corrected the stale pin SHA and the "sections at current pin" list; added the
  implementation-plan section so the item is directly implementable.
- Finished sequencing & dependencies review (plan): no children, so no `wl dep` edges to add; the
  in-slice order is recorded above with the fixture tests landing before the pin removal.
- Finished scope sizing review (plan): single leaf deliverable (~one test file + two doc lines);
  decomposition would create artificial children — recorded instead of creating them.
- Finished acceptance & testability review (plan): every AC is pass/fail; AC4 made checkable;
  AC2 and AC5 already carry explicit metrics.
- Finished polish & handoff review (plan): problem, constraints, key files and plan are copy-pasteable
  for `implement`; Q1 left as a non-blocking OPEN QUESTION for the producer.

- Finished completeness review: problem statement, ACs, constraints and key files added; no changes needed after first pass beyond adding the fixture strategy note.
- Finished capture-fidelity review: no user answers given (seed context + repo research only); Q1 recorded as OPEN QUESTION with recommendation.
- Finished related-work review: linked MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR, MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY, MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L, MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F, MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV, MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED; find-related report appended automatically.
- Finished risks & assumptions review: over-loosening mitigated by negative fixtures; engine-contract option isolated as scope-creep item.
- Finished polish & handoff: tightened wording; headline finalised.

## Related work (automated report from find-related)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F** – dev HEAD pin/pointer mismatch: engine-pin.json 01d6bcc1 vs core gitlink d907af9f (completed)
- **MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV** – Worktree core submodule checkouts lag the pin, so test runs compose a stale engine (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)

# Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

**Headline:** The Main Street story-line engine adapter omits the core `applyResourceDelta` seam, so option `cost` and `extraEffect` are never charged or applied.

Discovered-from: `MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY` (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Problem

Core `@story-line` resolves an option's declarative `cost` and `extraEffect` through the engine adapter's optional `applyResourceDelta` seam (`core/src/story-line/resolve.ts`). A legacy adapter without it is left untouched and appends the activity-log line *"Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied: the engine adapter does not implement applyResourceDelta."*

`mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`) implements `rng`, `applyEffect`, `getResources`, `appendLog`, `getActivityLog`, `getTemplate`, `getBaseTypeId`, `getChainScanCards` and `pushChainCard` — but **not** `applyResourceDelta`.

Consequences:

- A cost-gated option is filtered out of the presented list at draw time (`isOptionAffordable`), yet a *presented* cost option is never actually charged — so affordability never changes after paying.
- `extraEffect` deltas silently never land (options are inert where content expects a bonus/penalty).
- Any card using a cost or extra effect pollutes the activity log with the warning line above.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, the AI cost-aware policy (`MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY`) scores costs that the engine never collects and effects that never apply. The AI unit contract can still be satisfied (projection is a pure function), but end-to-end play with cost-bearing options is incorrect.

Secondary gap (same story, narrower): CSV `options` authoring has no syntax for `cost`/`extraEffect`, and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` `#/definitions/option` carries only `label`/`successorIds`/`effectPolicy`. So content cannot yet declare a cost — only registered options can. Authoring support should be its own item once enforcement exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` implements `applyResourceDelta(state, delta)`, applying `coins` and `reputation` deltas to `state.resourceBank` and keeping the ledger/score view consistent (same sync path `resolveEventOption` uses, e.g. `syncResourceBankToLedger`).
- A unit test proves a cost-bearing option deducts exactly `cost.coins`/`cost.reputation` on resolution, for both `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and `'skip'`.
- A unit test proves `extraEffect` deltas are applied for both effect policies, and that the resolution result's `coinChange`/`repChange` reports cost + extra effect + (for `apply`) the card effect.
- An integration test resolves a pending cost choice headlessly and asserts the activity log contains **no** "Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied" line.
- Undo of a resolved paid choice (snapshot command) restores the pre-payment resources; save/load round-trip preserves the post-payment balance.
- Existing behaviour with cost-free options is unchanged (storyline regression harness green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter, delegating to the existing state resource helpers and the ledger sync one-liner.
- Follow the settlement order documented in core: card effect (per `effectPolicy`) → cost → extra effect.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts` — add `applyResourceDelta`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` settlement/ledger sync + log assertions
- `src/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank` and ledger sync helpers
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — settlement order and warning contract (read-only)
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — resolution test home

## Notes

- `core/` is a pinned submodule — no core changes expected; if core needs a signature change, raise it as a core (`CG-`) item instead.
data.title: Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

# Reproduce pre-change soak-load failure baseline

## Headline

Reproduce the `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait failure on the pre-change baseline (dev tip before any deferral-helper extraction) at ≥ `nproc` (16) burners, recording the before-table as the evidence anchor for MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG. Runs through `/skill:test --type soak-load` (the policy-compliant harness) only — no ad-hoc vitest loops.

## Summary

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate fails exactly one wait at load ≥ ≈31 (≈2× oversubscription). This child re-runs that failing profile against the unmodified baseline in the item's worktree to (a) confirm the failure reproduces at the current dev tip (git state, not just the 2026-10-24 record), and (b) produce the before-table the parent AC requires. If the host cannot reach ambient load ≈31 with 16 burners, the achieved profile is recorded honestly instead of being re-labelled.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh` — the soak harness invoked via `/skill:test --type soak-load`.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — the failing wait lives here.
- `results/soak-browser-waits-<ts>.md` — written per run by the harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/skill:test --type soak-load` (16 burners, `--load`) runs on the pre-change dev tip; the outcome (pass or the failing wait) is recorded together with the achieved peak load, and the baseline commit hash is stated so the before/after comparison is exact.
- [ ] If the run fails, the failing wait is identified and confirmed to be `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` at its 40 000 ms budget — not another wait or a different failure mode.
- [ ] If the failure does not reproduce (host could not reach the ≥ ~31 peak-load envelope), that is recorded explicitly as "envelope not reached" with the achieved load, and the gap is carried into the post-change soak child rather than masked.
- [ ] Before-table posted as a comment on this item: burners, peak load, runs, per-run wall times, failure wait (if any) and the summary path (`results/soak-browser-waits-<ts>.md`), matching the 2026-10-24 table format on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L.
- [ ] No production or test code changed: `git status` clean apart from the soak evidence files under `results/`.
- [ ] Reliability proven, not assumed: pre-change `/skill:test --type soak-load` failure reproduced.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Verify the worktree is on the current dev tip (this child runs before any source change).
2. Run `/skill:test --type soak-load` (the `--load` profile uses `$nproc` burners).
3. Capture per-run wall times, peak load, and failure wait from the run output and the harness's markdown summary.
4. Post the before-table and baseline hash as a comment; do not modify sources.

# Intake brief: Dev-session browser console errors — `/api/transcripts` 404 and the dev-server drop cascade

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Cross-repo:** yes (`Tableau-Card-Engine` core + this repo) · **Discovered-from:** operator report (dev session, `vite --host` on `:3000`)

## Problem statement

A normal Main Street dev session fills the browser console with errors: every game-over `POST /api/transcripts` returns **HTTP 404** (the transcript persistence middleware exists in the engine but is never registered by this repo's generated `vite.config.ts`), and when the dev server dies mid-session the page floods with `[vite] server connection lost`, failed HMR WebSocket retries and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for all ~180 card SVG assets. The operator requirement is a clean dev-session console: no HTTP 404s from the app's own endpoints, no repeated warnings for expected conditions, and a documented, diagnosable signature (with evidence) for the two error classes that are not app defects.

## Users

- **Developers/agents running `npm run dev`** — must get a clean console so genuine errors are visible.
  - *User story:* "As a developer working on Main Street, I want a dev session where the console shows no 404s or error-class noise from the app, so that a red line in the console always means something is actually broken."
- **Anyone reading a session transcript / browser log for diagnosis** (agents auditing console output, the operator triaging a report) — must be able to tell app defects from environment/infrastructure artefacts.
  - *User story:* "As an operator triaging a pasted console log, I want each error class to be either fixed or explicitly documented as out-of-scope with a diagnostic procedure, so that I don't re-file it as a bug."
- **Core template maintainers** (Tableau-Card-Engine) — every scaffolded game repo must start with dev transcript persistence wired, so a re-scaffold cannot regress it.
  - *User story:* "As a core maintainer, I want `renderViteConfig` to emit the transcript-persist registration, so new game repos never ship a 404-ing `/api/transcripts`."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No `/api/transcripts` 404 in a dev session.** With `npm run dev` running, a game-over transcript save issues `POST /api/transcripts` and receives **HTTP 200**, and `data/transcripts/<gameType>/<gameType>-<ISO-timestamp>.json` is written; the browser console shows no `[TranscriptStore] Disk persistence POST returned HTTP 404`. Guarded by an automated test that loads the real `vite.config.ts` factory for `command: 'serve'` and asserts the `transcript-persist` plugin **is** registered, and is **not** registered when `process.env.VITEST` is set (mirroring `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts`), plus an in-process dev-server smoke that POSTs to `/api/transcripts` and asserts 200 + file creation under a temp `destRoot`.
2. **Scaffold template carries the same guard.** `renderViteConfig` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` emits the `transcriptPersistPlugin()` registration (dev-serve only, `!process.env.VITEST`-gated), and a core test asserts both the **rendered source** and the **on-disk generated** `vite.config.ts` contain it — so a `npm run scaffold` re-run cannot silently drop it (same pattern as the `resolve.dedupe` guard, MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL).
3. **Expected-condition logging is quiet.** The disk-persistence path issues its request only where the endpoint can exist (`import.meta.env.DEV`) and logs a non-2xx/missing-endpoint outcome **at most once per session at `console.debug`/`info`** — never a repeated `warn` for an expected absence — and the `csv-checksum.json` fetch-miss in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign` is downgraded the same way. Verified by unit tests asserting (a) at most one log call across repeated saves/failures, (b) no `console.warn`/`console.error` emitted on the expected-miss path.
4. **The two non-app error classes are resolved by evidence, not silence.** (a) `Uncaught (in promise) Error: A listener indicated an asynchronous response…` is verified to originate from a browser extension: an extension-free Chromium run of the existing Vitest `browser` project (whose `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` asserts a clean console on boot) produces no such error, and the finding is recorded in the work item as **out-of-scope with evidence**. (b) The dev-server-drop cascade (`[vite] server connection lost`, repeated `WebSocket connection to ws://<host>:3000/ failed`, `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for every card SVG / `csv-checksum.json`) is documented in a dev-server troubleshooting section of `docs/dev/testing.md` with: its signature; the fast triage (`ss -ltn | grep :3000` — no listener means the server is gone, not that assets are missing; the same assets return 200 from a live server); the likely causes on this host (swap exhaustion / memory pressure — 7.3 GB of 8 GB swap in use at report time, many `.worklog` worktrees, concurrent sibling dev servers and browser suites); and the remediation. Any host-level remediation is tracked in a linked follow-up item, not in app code.
5. **Tests and docs.** Changed-scope test gate green during implementation and the full project test suite green before the dev push; `docs/dev/testing.md` (and the `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence cross-reference, if the core contract changes) updated — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo:** the template half lives in the `core` submodule (`Tableau-Card-Engine`), which needs its own `CG-…` work item; this repo's `configs/engine-pin.json` pin must move after the core change lands (see MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV for the pin/lag rules, and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — a core worktree checkout lags the pin by design).
- **`vite.config.ts` is auto-generated** by the scaffold template; never hand-edit it without also changing `renderViteConfig`, or the next re-scaffold drops the fix.
- **Keep the VITEST gate.** The plugin intentionally does no file-system side effects during test runs (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence); the fix must not register it under `VITEST`.
- **No new runtime dependencies**; no change to the on-disk transcript contract (`data/transcripts/<game>/…`, consumed by `scripts/replay.ts` / `scripts/export-transcripts.ts`).
- **Do not weaken console assertions** as a way of passing: the e2e console guard must stay a real guard (adjusting benign-pattern lists is only acceptable for third-party/browser noise with recorded justification).

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` exports `transcriptPersistPlugin()` + a bounded `POST /api/transcripts` handler (body cap, rate limit, atomic-ish write to `data/transcripts/`) — the middleware is correct and battle-tested in core.
- `core/vite.config.ts` registers it: `...(command === 'serve' && !process.env.VITEST ? [transcriptPersistPlugin()] : [])`.
- **This repo's `vite.config.ts` imports only `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`** from that module and never registers the plugin — verified live: a fresh `vite --port 3000` session returns `HTTP 404` for `POST /api/transcripts` while `/`, every card SVG and `csv-checksum.json` return `HTTP 200`.
- `core/src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` → `postToDisk()` fire-and-forgets `fetch('/api/transcripts')` and `console.warn`s on any non-OK response — so every game-over logs a 404 warn whenever the plugin is absent (dev misconfiguration, Vitest browser mode, production build, Electron).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` (~L230) `console.warn`s on a `csv-checksum.json` fetch throw.
- The dev-server drop is environmental: swap is 7.3 GB / 8 GB consumed on this host, 23 `.worklog` worktrees exist, and sibling repos (`AI_Hell`, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) were running their own `vite --host` dev servers plus a browser test suite concurrently at the time of the report. `docs/dev/testing.md` already documents the analogous ENOSPC/environmental class and its triage (reference MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C) — same treatment applies here.
- `installHook.js` appears in the operator's stack traces; this repo has no React and no `chrome.runtime` usage, so the message-channel error is extension-origin.

## Desired change

1. Register `transcriptPersistPlugin()` in this repo's `vite.config.ts`, gated on dev-serve and not under `VITEST` (the config factory callback must take `command`).
2. Mirror that registration in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig` (core repo, own `CG-…` item) + a core template guard test.
3. Add a game-repo guard test for the registration contract (serve vs VITEST) and, for real coverage of the wiring, an in-process dev-server smoke asserting `POST /api/transcripts` → 200 with a temp `destRoot`.
4. Make expected-condition logging quiet and once-per-session: gate `postToDisk` on `import.meta.env.DEV`, and downgrade the non-2xx/miss path plus the `csv-checksum.json` fetch miss to a single debug/info log.
5. Document the dev-server-drop signature, triage steps and likely causes in `docs/dev/testing.md`; record the extension-origin verification for the message-channel error; file/link a follow-up for host remediation if the kill cause proves host-level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite.config.ts` — import `transcriptPersistPlugin`; take `command` in the factory; register it dev-serve-only behind `!process.env.VITEST`
- `tests/tooling/vite-transcript-plugin-registration.test.ts` — **new** guard (plugin present for `serve`, absent under `VITEST`) + in-process dev-server smoke POST → 200 + file written
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderViteConfig` emits the registration (core repo change)
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — assert rendered template **and** on-disk generated config carry the registration (core repo)
- `core/src/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.ts` — `postToDisk`: `import.meta.env.DEV` gate + log-once at debug/info
- `tests/core-engine/transcript/TranscriptStore.test.ts` (core) — log-volume assertions (≤1 log across repeated failures; no warn on expected path)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — `csv-checksum.json` fetch-miss `console.warn` → `console.debug`
- `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` — extend/confirm it also covers the transcript-persistence path (no 404 warn, no message-channel error)
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — new "dev server died: WS failures + `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`" troubleshooting section (signature, triage, causes, remediation)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Transcript Persistence cross-reference for the game-repo registration contract (only if the contract text changes)

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** (completed) — *Scaffold template must emit `resolve.dedupe` in generated `vite.config.ts`*: the exact cross-repo precedent for this fix (generated file + `renderViteConfig` + template guard), including how the core work item and pin bump were handled.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** (completed) — *Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs*: the established pattern for classifying a dev-server failure as environmental and documenting (not coding around) it.
- **MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C** (completed) — the ENOSPC troubleshooting entry in `docs/dev/testing.md` that the new dev-server-drop section should mirror in tone and structure.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** (open, low) — *Port Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) to sibling game repos' generated `vite.config.ts`*: same "generated config drift" family; this item's template change should be reviewed against it so the two template edits do not conflict.
- **MS-0MV26MOWT004ZCQC** (completed) — *Console noise when running the tutorial (tf factory + zone collision warnings)*: prior art for "console must be clean" as a testable contract.
- **MS-0MUTU19SF007791K** (completed) — *Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start*: explains the `Regenerated N card SVGs` info lines (and why 175 vs 185 is a card-pack/CSV change, not an error).
- **MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0** (open) — *Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos*: touch-point if the template is regenerated/inspected here.
- Docs: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Transcript Persistence (endpoint contract + VITEST/rate-limit rationale); `docs/dev/testing.md` (troubleshooting section conventions); `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (module doc-comment: memory-safety bounds, `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — template drift (high impact, low likelihood once guarded):** editing only this repo's generated `vite.config.ts` leaves the next `npm run scaffold` broken. *Mitigation:* template change + template guard test in core (AC2).
- **Risk — cross-repo sequencing:** the core change needs its own `CG-…` item and a pin bump here; doing the game-repo half first means a transient period where `core` lags. *Mitigation:* land the core template change first, then re-pin and regenerate (MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV rules); document the order in the child items.
- **Risk — silencing real errors:** downgrading logs can hide genuine failures. *Mitigation:* log-once at debug/info, keep an error-level log for *unexpected* failures (non-DEV builds, 5xx), and assert the distinction in tests.
- **Risk — Vitest browser mode hits the same 404 path** (`VITEST` disables the plugin) and could newly fail a console-clean assertion. *Mitigation:* the `import.meta.env.DEV` gate removes the request entirely under test/prod builds; assert it in the unit test rather than adding the 404 to a benign list.
- **Risk — scope creep into host remediation** (swap pressure, orphaned dev servers, 23 worktrees). *Mitigation:* per operator decision this item documents + diagnoses only; host remediation becomes a linked follow-up item (`machine-hygiene` domain).
- **Assumption:** the operator's browser has a devtools-type extension loaded (evidence: `installHook.js` in the stack); the message-channel error therefore cannot be eliminated from app code and is closed by verification + documentation (AC4a).
- **Assumption:** no product code currently depends on transcript disk persistence; the fix restores a dev-only convenience plus a console-hygiene contract.
- **Out of scope (record as follow-ups, not scope):** a dev-server supervisor/auto-restart wrapper; swapping this host's workloads; a general console-error lint gate for all dev sessions; the 175→185 SVG count difference (card-pack activation, not an error).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Scope of the dev-server drop cascade** (WS failures + `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` + downstream warns) — (a) treat as machine-environmental: document the diagnosis and link a separate host-remediation item, or (b) treat as an app bug requiring code-level resilience to a downed dev server?
  - **Answer (operator): (a)** — document as environmental with diagnosis; keep host remediation separate. Source: interactive reply (`wl reviewed` round 1).
  - Research: a live `vite --port 3000` probe returns 200 for every asset the report lists as `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`; host shows 7.3 GB/8 GB swap consumed, 23 `.worklog` worktrees, and concurrent sibling dev servers/browser suites.
- **Q2: Cross-repo core template fix** — fix this repo's `vite.config.ts` and the core scaffold template, or game-repo only?
  - **Answer (operator): both.** Source: interactive reply (`wl reviewed` round 1).
  - Research: precedent MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL (cross-repo "generated config drift" intake; core item + pin bump). `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderViteConfig` currently emits no transcript plugin and no `command` parameter.
- **Q3: The extension message-channel error** — verify it is extension-origin in a clean Chromium and record as out-of-scope, or must this item eliminate it regardless of origin?
  - **Answer (operator): verify + record.** Source: interactive reply (`wl reviewed` round 1).
  - Research: `installHook.js` is a browser-extension hook; this repo has no React and no `chrome.runtime` usage; the extension-free `browser` project boots the game cleanly.

---

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** – Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed)
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** – Port Vite watcher-ignore (server.watch.ignored) to sibling game repos' generated vite.config.ts (open)

Coordinator handoff (epic drive MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG, attempt 1 failed) - producer-relevant environment facts.

**Attempt 1 outcome:** the driven session ran ~1.7 h and then exited 1 with `503 "All providers exhausted"` (transient model-provider failure, not a work-item problem). Item was reset to `open`; worktree is clean. Retrying.

**Host state observed during attempt 1 (measured, not assumed):**
- Ambient load average swung 10.4 - 47.1 over the attempt (many sibling agent suites running on this shared 16-core host).
- The test-concurrency semaphore has 2 slots and both were held by sibling suites for the *entire* attempt: 55 consecutive gate checks over 2430 s all reported `free_slots=0/2`.
- The attempt's gated launcher waited its bounded 2430 s for `load<20 AND free_slot>=1`, launched anyway (correct, honest behaviour), and `run_tests.py` then refused with `test concurrency slot busy` because the default `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` is 600 s and the launcher did not set it.

**Guidance for this attempt (do not re-derive):**
1. Do **not** hand-roll a slot-gating launcher. Let `run_tests.py` do the waiting: export `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=5400` (and optionally `TEST_LOCK_JITTER=0.4`) before `/skill:test --type soak-load`. The runner then blocks for a slot instead of failing fast with `slot busy`.
2. Budget realistically: a quiet-host browser run is 58-95 s and 129-137 s under load, so `--runs 5 --load` needs one slot for roughly 10-20 min once acquired, plus up to `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` of slot waiting. `timeoutPerCommand` is 1800 s in `.pi/test-config.json`, so consider a single-run/short profile only if a 5-run soak cannot fit inside it — and record whichever profile you actually achieved, honestly.
3. Baseline facts already established in attempt 1 (reuse, do not re-run): worktree HEAD == `origin/dev` == `77d1dd31185f80884e1ce736ea8c6b8c41e62766` (the pre-change dev tip, i.e. the baseline this child must measure).
